slides.teacher_cue: New sound — long /oʊ/. Two spellings: oa appears in the middle of a word (boat, road, coat), ow appears at the end of a word (snow, flow, grow). Same position rule as ai/ay: oa in the middle, ow at the end. Note: ow can also make /aʊ/ (as in cow) — that pattern comes later. For now: ow = /oʊ/.
slides.expected_response: Students produce /oʊ/ cleanly and understand the oa/ow position rule.
slides.correction_move: Model the position rule: oa in the middle — boat, road. ow at the end — snow, flow. Students sort. Preview: ow can also say /aʊ/ — but we will learn that later.
slides.observation_note: Watch for ow/oa spelling confusion and for pure /oʊ/ production — not diphthong drift.

slides.teacher_cue: Say boat — a vessel on water. oa in the middle. Reveal and blend.
slides.expected_response: Students say boat orally, connect meaning, then blend on the card.
slides.correction_move: Model boat orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for the oa vowel team in the middle and for /oʊ/ production.

slides.teacher_cue: Say road — a path for vehicles. Confirm /r/ onset and oa vowel team. Reveal and blend.

slides.correction_move: Model road orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for /l/ on /r/ and for the oa vowel team.

slides.observation_note: Watch for /p/ on /f/ and /l/ vs /r/ in onset.

slides.correction_move: Model snow orally again, reveal and blend.
slides.observation_note: Watch for the ow spelling at the end — contrast with oa in the middle.

slides.teacher_cue: Say grow — to get bigger. gr onset, ow at the end. Confirm /r/ in onset. Reveal and blend.
